You’re not wrong that it’s a chunk of money for “a couple hours and some wire,” so it’s smart to sanity‑check it.

Here’s what I can see from their profiles:

Licensing / insurance
- Liberty Electric Services (quote ~$540)  
  - Certifications: “Licensed Master Electrician”, “Bonded & Insured”, “OSHA 10 Certified”  
  - Insurance flag: true  
  - 17 years in business, works regularly in Center City / Philadelphia.  

- Keystone Power Pros (quote ~$475)  
  - Certifications: “Licensed Electrician”, “Bonded & Insured”  
  - Insurance flag: true  
  - 6 years in business, also lists Philadelphia/Center City as a service area.  

So both are licensed and insured outfits that routinely work in Philly.

How “hard” are these numbers?
- These are structured estimates: each quote includes a defined service fee, parts, labor, and tax for “one new dedicated 120V circuit from existing panel in the same space, for office loads.”  
- As long as:
  - The panel really is in good condition and has space for the new breaker, and  
  - The run is reasonably straightforward (no surprise fishing through inaccessible spaces, no code issues, no panel upgrade needed),  
  then they should stick close to the quoted total.  

When could they add on?
- Situations that typically increase cost:
  - Panel has no free spaces or is in poor shape and must be repaired/upgraded.
  - The cable run turns out to be much longer or requires opening/patching a lot of finished walls/ceilings.
  - You change the scope on-site (e.g., add outlets, ask for multiple circuits, etc.).

Given your description (panel in same space, standard office loads), this job is right in their wheelhouse, so extra charges would usually only come up if they find something unexpected or you expand the scope.

If you want to push the cost down further, a few options:
- We can pull 1–2 more quotes to see if anyone comes in lower.  
- Or you can prioritize:  
  - Keystone: cheaper at ~$475, slightly shorter warranty.  
  - Liberty: costs more but has a stronger 1‑year parts / 90‑day labor warranty and higher rating.

What would you like to do next?  
- Go with Keystone at 2–5 pm on Fri 12/12,  
- Go with Liberty at 1–4 pm or 4–7 pm that day,  
- Or have me shop around for a couple more quotes before you decide?</action>
